title: Binary to decimal
stem: What is the binary number 10100000 in decimal?
answers: That counts only the leftmost bit. The third bit adds 32.
Correct. The bits worth 128 and 32 are on: 128 + 32 = 160.
That's 11000000, with the 128 and 64 bits on. Here the second bit is off and the third is on.
That's 01010000. Start the values at 128, not 64.

title: Decimal to binary
stem: Which binary number equals the decimal number 10?
answers: That's 4 + 1 = 5, half of 10.
Correct. The bits worth 8 and 2 are on: 8 + 2 = 10.

title: Bit values in an octet
stem: In one octet of an IPv4 address, what are the values of the eight bit positions, from left to right?
answers: Those are the right values in the wrong order. The leftmost bit is the biggest.
Correct. Each position is double the one to its right, starting at 128.
255 is the value of all eight bits together, not one position.
Binary positions double; they don't halve from 100.

title: Largest octet value
stem: What is the largest decimal value one octet of an IPv4 address can hold?
answers: There are 256 possible values, but they run from 0 to 255.
128 is just the leftmost bit. All eight bits on is larger.
That needs more than eight bits.
Correct. All eight bits on: 128 + 64 + 32 + 16 + 8 + 4 + 2 + 1 = 255.

title: Prefix length
stem: A network is written as 192.168.10.0/24. What does the /24 tell you?
answers: The network has 24 usable host addresses
A /24 actually leaves 8 host bits, which gives 254 usable addresses.
The first 24 bits are the network part
Correct. The prefix length counts the network bits; the remaining 8 bits identify hosts.
The router is at address .24
The prefix length says nothing about where the router is.
The address is in the 24th subnet of the company
It's a count of network bits, not a subnet number.

title: Mask for a /24
stem: Which subnet mask matches a /24 prefix?
answers: That's /16: only two octets of ones.
That's /32, a single host.
Correct. 24 ones make three full octets of 255, then a 0.
A mask is made of ones from the left. 24 is the count of those ones, not an octet value.

title: Hosts on a /24
stem: How many usable host addresses does a /24 network have?
answers: Correct. 8 host bits give 256 addresses; the network address and the broadcast address can't go to hosts, leaving 254.
That's every address, including the network and broadcast addresses, which hosts can't use.
Two addresses are reserved, not one: the network address and the broadcast address.
24 is the number of network bits, not hosts.

title: Same network or not
stem: Two computers have the addresses 10.1.1.20/24 and 10.1.2.20/24. Are they on the same network?
answers: Yes, because both start with 10.1
With a /24, the first three octets must match. The third octets are 1 and 2.
Yes, because both end in .20
The last octet is the host part. Matching host numbers don't put them on the same network.
It depends on the default gateway
The gateway doesn't change which network an address is on. The address and mask decide that.
No, the third octets differ
Correct. A /24 network uses the first three octets: 10.1.1 and 10.1.2 are different networks, so they need a router between them.

title: Private address
stem: Which of these is a private IPv4 address that a home or office network might use inside?
answers: That's a public address (a well-known public DNS server).
Correct. 192.168.0.0/16 is one of the private ranges, along with 10.0.0.0/8 and 172.16.0.0/12.
That's public. The private range is 192.168, not 200.168.
Close, but the private range is 172.16 to 172.31. 172.32 is public.

title: No DHCP answer
stem: A laptop shows the address 169.254.33.7. What does that usually mean?
answers: The laptop has a static address set by the help desk
Help desks don't assign this range. It's what a device gives itself.
The laptop is connected to the internet through a VPN
A VPN address comes from the VPN, not this range.
No DHCP server answered its request
Correct. 169.254.x.x is APIPA: the device picked its own address because DHCP didn't respond. Session 4 covers why.
The laptop has an IPv6 address
169.254.33.7 is IPv4. IPv6 addresses use hexadecimal and colons.
